name: Three-player Kuhn poker: does the Szafron-Gibson-Sturtevant family contain every Nash equilibrium (on the path of play)?
compute_profile: laptop-hours (exact algebra and global nonconvex searches over a 48-parameter game); a completeness proof is mostly pure thought plus case-split computer algebra
statement: Three-player Kuhn poker (introduced by Abou Risk and Szafron, 2010; rules as in Szafron, Gibson and Sturtevant, AAMAS 2013, Section 2): a 4-card deck {1,2,3,4}, each player antes 1 chip and gets one card, one betting round with a single fixed bet of 1 chip (check or bet; fold or call when facing a bet; no raises), P1 acts first, showdown among the players who have not folded. A behavioural profile is 48 numbers a_jk, b_jk, c_jk (P1, P2, P3 holding card j in betting situation k = 1..4 of the paper's Table 1). Szafron, Gibson and Sturtevant derived analytically a parameterized family of Nash equilibria (their Tables 2 and 3: three sub-families c11 = 0, 0 < c11 < 1/2 and c11 = 1/2, with 4, 4 and 5 free parameters) with payoffs u1 = -(1+2*beta)/48, u2 = -1/48, u3 = (1+beta)/24, where beta = max{b11, b21} is in [0, 1/4], and in which P1 always checks first. Their conclusion (Section 8) reads: 'It remains open as to whether there exist other three-player Kuhn equilibrium profiles that do not belong to this family.' Wikipedia's Kuhn poker page still says (2026-10-14): 'It is not known if this equilibrium family covers all Nash equilibria for the game.' Ganzfried, Nowak and Pinales (2018) repeat that there 'may be others beyond those in the family'. Ganzfried (Games 17(1):9, 2026; arXiv:2509.25618v3) reported an equilibrium from Gurobi nonconvex QCP (reported deviation gain at most 1.4e-17; that numerical residual alone is not an exact certificate) of the game with dominated actions removed. It agrees with the family except at two information sets that are reached with probability zero: P1 holding card 3 after check-bet-fold always folds instead of calling with probability 1/2, and P3 holding card 3 facing P1's bet after P2 folds calls with probability 1/2. He concludes that 'additional Nash equilibria exist beyond those in the infinite family previously computed (though perhaps they only differ from the family off the path of play)'. Ganzfried (arXiv:2606.25997v2, June 2026) solves the full game exactly in 1.16 s. Gambit's logit solution and Billingham's numerical continuation (arXiv:1802.04670) also land in the family. The cited work reports off-path differences; the present target asks whether any equilibrium differs from every family member ON the path of play. A candidate completeness proof was closed in PR #201 pending a novelty check of Prisner (2014), chapter "Example: VNM POKER and KUHN POKER", and independent review. Completeness and novelty are not established here. The earlier page review could not retrieve the Wikipedia status source (HTTP 403); the cited papers provide the historical comparison.
success_criterion: Settle the question of Szafron, Gibson and Sturtevant (AAMAS 2013, Section 8) in its on-path form, for the game exactly as defined in their Section 2 (cards 1..4, ante 1, bet 1, acting order P1, P2, P3, the betting rules stated there). Direction: settle, either way. EITHER (A) COUNTEREXAMPLE: an explicit profile sigma given as 48 rational action probabilities, such that (1) sigma is an exact Nash equilibrium: for each player i, the exact best-response value against sigma_-i equals u_i(sigma), both computed in exact rational arithmetic over all 24 deals; and (2) sigma differs from every member of the family of Tables 2-3 ON THE PATH OF PLAY, shown by at least one of these witnesses: (W1) u2(sigma) != -1/48; (W2) the payoff vector is not (-(1+2*beta)/48, -1/48, (1+beta)/24) for any beta in [0, 1/4]; (W3) P1 bets first with positive probability with some card (some a_j1 > 0); (W4) an explicit argument, re-derived from Tables 2-3, that for each of the three sub-families no member assigns sigma's action probabilities at every information set that sigma reaches with positive probability. A profile that differs from the family only at information sets of zero reach probability does NOT count (Ganzfried 2026 already found one). OR (B) PROOF: a machine-checked proof (Lean, Coq or Isabelle; no sorry, admit or new axioms), or an exact-arithmetic certificate verified by a checker that shares no code with the prover, that every Nash equilibrium of the game coincides, at every information set it reaches with positive probability, with some member of the family of Tables 2-3 (equivalently, induces the same distribution over terminal histories as some member).

partial_wins.statement: A machine-checked proof, or an exact certificate verified by an independent checker, that P2's expected payoff equals -1/48 in EVERY Nash equilibrium of three-player Kuhn poker. This extends the family's headline property to all equilibria; a single exact equilibrium with u2 != -1/48 is instead a full win under (A).
A machine-checked proof, or an exact certificate verified by an independent checker, that in EVERY Nash equilibrium P1 never bets first with any card (a_j1 = 0 for j = 1..4).

verification_method: Write an exact evaluator of about 150 lines (Python fractions.Fraction). Enumerate the 24 ordered deals and the betting tree, compute u_i(sigma), and compute each player's best-response value by backward induction over that player's 16 information sets (card x situation) using opponent-reach-weighted counterfactual values, all in exact arithmetic. sigma is an equilibrium iff BR_i = u_i for i = 1, 2, 3. Validate the evaluator and the transcription of Tables 2-3 on the family itself: sampled members of each sub-family must be exact equilibria with the stated payoffs (Theorem 2 of the paper). Then check the claimed witness W1-W4. For (B) and the partial wins, build in a clean environment, run #print axioms (or Print Assumptions), and check that the formal game model reproduces the family's payoffs and equilibrium property before trusting any statement proved about it.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical proposal date preserved. No fresh source request was made during final preparation. The earlier page review could not retrieve the Wikipedia status source (HTTP 403); the cited papers provide the historical comparison. A candidate proof was closed in V3R1T4S PR #201 pending a novelty check of Prisner (2014), chapter "Example: VNM POKER and KUHN POKER", and an independent review. This does not establish completeness.
angles: Aim straight at a witness: add a_41 >= delta (P1 opens with the best card), a_11 >= delta (P1 opens as a bluff), or u2 >= -1/48 + delta to the nonlinear-complementarity equilibrium conditions, and solve globally with an open-source spatial branch-and-bound solver (SCIP). Use Ganzfried's finite bounds on slack and multiplier variables (arXiv:2606.25997), which cut the full-game solve from more than 24 h to about 1 s. Rationalize any solution and verify it exactly.

Support enumeration plus exact algebra: fix which information sets are reached and which actions are mixed; each case is a system of multilinear equalities and inequalities in at most 27 free parameters (Theorem 1 already fixes 21 parameters when reached). Solve the cases with Groebner bases or real-root isolation (msolve, Singular, sympy).

Think like the 2-player game: in 2-player Kuhn, P1 bets the best card with probability 3*alpha and bluffs the worst with alpha. Test whether an analogous opening (a_41 > 0 balanced by a_11 > 0), with P2 and P3 calling ranges re-balanced, can be supported. The family was read off Monte Carlo CFR solutions run with different random seeds, and CFR carries no convergence guarantee in 3-player games, so it may have missed whole regions.

For the proof direction, follow the case structure of the paper's appendix (four lemmas for Theorem 1). First prove p2 (P1 never opens): every case with some a_j1 > 0 must yield a profitable deviation. Then p1. The rest of the family's structure should follow by restricting to P1-never-opens profiles.
pitfalls: Off-path differences already exist (Ganzfried 2026) and do not count; the claim must change what happens with positive probability.

Card and parameter labels differ between sources: the paper uses cards 1..4, Ganzfried uses J, Q, K, A. One of Ganzfried's off-path parameters is labelled c32 although the situation he describes (P1 bets, P2 folds) is situation 3 of the paper's Table 1. Map situations from the paper's Table 1, not from parameter names.
Take the parameter ranges from the paper (beta <= 1/4), not from secondary summaries.
Solver output with tolerance 1e-13 to 1e-17 is not an exact equilibrium. Rationalize and verify in exact arithmetic.

Nash equilibrium, not a refinement: off-path behaviour may be arbitrary as long as no unilateral deviation pays. Do not impose sequential rationality, and do not discard equilibria because they play weakly dominated actions at unreached information sets.
The PDF renders the fractions in Tables 2-3 badly. Validate any transcription against Theorem 2 (family members are equilibria with the stated payoffs) before using it to judge non-membership.
Check papers citing Szafron et al. 2013 (and Ganzfried's 2025-2026 papers) before claiming; the question is cited by an active line of exact-solver work.

Before attacking or claiming, check Prisner (2014), chapter "Example: VNM POKER and KUHN POKER", for prior results covering the same three-player rules and on-path question. PR #201 was closed pending that novelty check and independent review; the candidate is not established.
